'''Jack Marvin Williams''' (born 26 September 1938) is an American chemist who contributed to the development of [[organic superconductors]].

== Early life and career ==
Born in [[Delta, Colorado]], he earned his BSc from [[Lewis & Clark College]] in 1960 and his PhD in physical and inorganic chemistry from [[Washington State University]] in 1966.<ref name=USA>{{Cite book |title = American Men & Women of Science |editor=Jaques Cattell Press |publisher = R. R. Bowker Co. |edition = 16th|volume = VII|year=1986| page = 643 }}</ref>

After obtaining his PhD, he served as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Argonne National Laboratory]] (ANL) in Illinois for two years. He was promoted to the positions of assistant chemist in 1968, associate chemist in 1970, chemist in 1972, and senior chemist in 1977.<ref name=WHO>{{cite book|title=Who's Who in America, 1982-1983|volume=2|edition=42|publisher=Marquis Who's Who Inc.|publication-place=Chicago, Illinois|page=3577|year=1982}}</ref> Additionally, he led the chemistry, material science, and technology divisions from 1977 onwards.<ref name=USA></ref>

He also served as a visiting guest professor at the [[University of Missouri]] in 1980 and 1981 and at the [[University of Copenhagen]] in 1980 and 1985. He was also the chairman of the [[Gordon Research Conferences]] (Inorganic Chemistry) in 1980.<ref name=USA></ref>

He retired from ANL in 1997 for health reasons.<ref name=MOL>{{cite journal |doi=10.1080/713738690
|title=The search for new superconductors at argonne national Laboratory|year=2002|last1=Geiser|first1=Urs|last2=Kini|first2=Aravinda M.|last3=Schlueter|first3=John A.|last4=Wang|first4=H. Hau|last5=Williams|first5=Jack M.|journal=Molecular Crystals and Liquid Crystals|volume=380|issue=1|pages=29-35|bibcode=2002MCLC..380...29G|osti=813787}}</ref>

== Research ==
His early research focused on elucidating the properties of chemical bonds using [[X-ray diffraction]] and [[neutron diffraction]].<ref name=MOL></ref><ref>{{cite report|editor-last=Williams|editor-first=Jack W.|title=Present Needs and Future Trends in Neutron Crystallography and Spectroscopy|year=1978|publisher=Argonne National Laboratory|osti=12236032|osti-access=free|doi=10.2172/12236032|doi-access=free}}</ref> Attending the International Conference on Synthetic Metals in 1979 in [[Helsingør|Helsingør, Denmark]], where [[Klaus Bechgaard]] and [[Denis Jérome]] reported on the superconducting behavior of (TMTSF)<sub>2</sub>PF<sub>6</sub>, introduced him to superconductivity in organic [[charge-transfer complexes]].<ref name=MOL></ref> Upon returning to ANL, he built up a
program in [[organic conductor]]s and superconductors.<ref name=MOL></ref>

He played a role in the development of [[organic superconductors]] in the United States. Building his background in structural and inorganic chemistry, he proposed design approaches for inorganic anions in organic charge-transfer complexes,<ref>{{cite book|last1=Williams|first1=Jack M.|last2=Kini|first2=Aravinda M.|last3=Geiser|first3=Urs|last4=Wang|first4=Hau H.|last5=Douglas Carlson|first5=K.|last6=Kwok|first6=W. K.|last7=Vandervoort|first7=K. Hau|last4=Wang|first5=Urs|last5=Geiser|first6=John A.|last6=Schlueter|first7=Arthur J.|last7=Schultz|first8=James E.|last8=Schirber|first9= Eugene L.|last9=Venturini|first10=Donald L.|last10=Overmyer|first11=Myung-Hwan|last11=Whangbo|chapter=Structure-Property Relationships in Radical-Cation (Electron-Donor Molecule) and Anion-Based (Including Fullerides) Organic Superconductors and their Use in the Design of New Materials|pages=539-551|title=Materials and Crystallographic Aspects of HT<sub>c</sub>-Superconductivity|year=1994|edition=1|editor-last=Kaldis|editor-first=E.|series=NATO Science Series E|volume=263|publisher=Springer|publication-place=Dordrecht|doi=10.1007/978-94-011-1064-8_26|osti=10182370|osti-access=free}}</ref> which contributed to the discovery of several organic superconductors, including κ-type BEDT-TTF salts, by his research group.<ref name=MOL></ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Stewart|first1=G. == Awards ==
In 1989, he received an Alumni Achievement Award from Washington State University in recognition of his "outstanding accomplishments in research and service in the field of chemistry, bringing recognition to his alma mater".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://screens.wsu.edu/alumniwallofhonor/alumni-achievement/|title=Alumni Achievement Award|website=Washington State University Alumni Association|accessdate=26 September 2026}}</ref>
